newsitem.title: USA: LESLIE-ADM PEGS US CORN 9.656 BLN BU, SOY 2.71 BLN.
newsitem.headline: LESLIE-ADM PEGS US CORN 9.656 BLN BU, SOY 2.71 BLN.

text.p: The Conrad Leslie-ADM Elevator survey on Friday estimated U.S. corn production based on Aug 1 conditions at 9.656 billion bushels and soybeans at 2.713 billion bushels.
The estimates are based on inquiries with 1,250 grain elevators in the Corn Belt.
The estimates compare with USDA's July estimates of 9.70 billion bushels for corn and 2.69 billion bu for soybeans. U.S. corn production in 1996 totalled 9.293 billion bu and soybeans 2.382 billion.
U.S. average production for the past five years has been 8.517 billion bu corn and 2.227 billion bu soybeans.
Leslie pegged average corn yield at 130.5 bushels per acre against the five year average of 122.3 and last year's 127.1 bushels.
Leslie pegged end-season carryout on August 31, 1998, at 1.142 billion bushels, against 916 million a year earlier, based on current demand estimates by the USDA.
Leslie pegged average soybean yield at 38.9 bushels per acre against the five year average of 36.9 and last year's 37.6 bushels.

Based on USDA demand and stocks estimates, Leslie pegged end-stocks of soybeans on Aug 31, 1998, at 303 million bushels compared to 125 million on Aug 31, 1997, based on current demand estimates by USDA.
Leslie said his report used USDA's June 30 acreage-for-harvest estimates of 74.02 million acres of corn and 69.83 million acres of soybeans.
